parameters.content:
## AetherForge Daily Tweet Engine

Three independent flows, each with its own Schedule Trigger — activate the whole workflow and all three run on their own cadence.

**Setup (once):**
1. Credentials → create **X OAuth1 API** (developer.x.com → your app → Keys and Tokens → API Key/Secret + Access Token/Secret, app permission = Read and Write). Used by every X node below.
2. Credentials → create **GitHub Contents Token** (fine-grained PAT, Contents: Read and write, scoped to this one repo only). Used by every GitHub node below.
3. In the two "Set - Your X Account" nodes (Reply flow + Metrics flow), fill in your numeric X user ID and handle. Find your numeric ID once via a site like tweeterid.com, or by calling `GET https://api.twitter.com/2/users/by/username/<handle>` yourself with the same credential in a REST client.
4. Click each X/GitHub node once and hit "Test step" before activating — confirms the credential actually works before it's live.

**Cost control (read this before activating the Reply/Metrics flows):** posting tweets is normally free, but reading mentions and metrics is billed under X's pay-as-you-go pricing once you're past Free-tier limits. Set a hard monthly spending cap in your X developer billing settings — that cap, not this workflow, is your real backstop. Both read flows are scheduled conservatively (mentions every 30 min, metrics once/day) and use since_id/small max_results to avoid re-fetching the same data twice, but check your actual per-call pricing before leaving this active for a long stretch.

**Reply flow is fully autonomous by request — no human review step.** It posts immediately using a small template bank (no LLM call, so no added API cost). Everything it sends is logged read-only in the Command Deck's Mission Log → Replies tab so you can audit after the fact.

### Flow A — Post the queue
Same flow as before, now posting for real to X (was a placeholder "OpenTweet" endpoint).

nodes.name: Fetch Content Queue (GitHub)
nodes.notes: Default (non-raw) Accept header — response includes both `content` (base64) and `sha`. Retries 3x on transient failures before giving up for this run.

nodes.name: Post Tweet
nodes.notes: Real X API v2 tweet creation (replaces the old OpenTweet placeholder). Deliberately NOT using retryOnFail: retrying a create-tweet call on a timeout risks double-posting if the first attempt actually succeeded but the response was lost. A genuine failure here waits for the next scheduled run instead of retrying blind.

nodes.name: Mark Posted (GitHub commit)
nodes.notes: Safe to retry: idempotent write, and X already has the post regardless of whether this commit succeeds first try.

parameters.content:
### Flow B — Auto-reply to mentions
Fully autonomous, per your call: no review step. Reads/writes data/x-automation-state.json for its since_id cursor + a read-only log the Command Deck displays.

nodes.name: Set - Your X Account (Replies)
nodes.notes: Fill in once. Numeric user ID (not your @handle) — X's mentions endpoint needs it.

nodes.name: Fetch Automation State (GitHub)
nodes.notes: continueOnFail is intentional: this file doesn't exist until the first successful run, and a 404 here must not kill the workflow. The Code node downstream treats a missing/errored response as "no prior state".

nodes.name: Get Mentions
nodes.notes: READ call — costs money under X pay-as-you-go once past Free-tier limits. since_id (from "Decode Automation State") keeps every poll fetching only new mentions, never re-billing for ones already seen. The since_id clause is only appended to the URL when a cursor actually exists, so the very first run (no prior state) never sends an empty/invalid since_id that X could reject.

nodes.name: Post Reply
nodes.notes: No retryOnFail, same double-post reasoning as Post Tweet in Flow A. This is the fully-autonomous send — nothing reviews this text before it goes out.

nodes.name: Commit Automation State (GitHub)
nodes.notes: sha is omitted (undefined) on the very first-ever run since the file doesn't exist yet — the GitHub Contents API creates it instead of updating.

parameters.content:
### Flow C — Daily metrics sync
Once a day (deliberately not more often — this is 2 more billed reads under pay-as-you-go). Writes data/live-metrics.json, which the Command Deck reads read-only.

nodes.name: Set - Your X Account (Metrics)
nodes.notes: Fill in once — just your @handle, no @ symbol.

nodes.name: Get User
nodes.notes: READ call, billed under pay-as-you-go past Free-tier limits — this is why the whole flow runs once/day rather than more often.

nodes.name: Get Recent Tweets
nodes.notes: Second READ call of this daily run. public_metrics (likes/retweets/replies/quotes) is included at every X API access level; impression_count needs a higher access level and may be absent — the Code node downstream degrades gracefully (treats it as 0) rather than erroring if so.

nodes.name: Fetch Existing Live Metrics (for sha)
nodes.notes: continueOnFail intentional: doesn't exist on the very first run. Only used to grab `sha` for the update below.

parameters.content:
### Flow D — Curated engagement scan
Human-in-the-loop by design, not a missing feature: genuinely sharp, non-generic replies to high-profile accounts need real judgment an LLM-free workflow can't fake. This only finds candidates and writes them to data/reply-candidates.json — the Command Deck shows them, you write and send the actual reply yourself.

nodes.name: Resolve Account IDs
nodes.notes: One batched READ call resolves all 16 handles to numeric IDs at once — far cheaper than 16 separate lookups.

nodes.name: Get Recent Tweets Per Account
nodes.notes: One READ call per curated account, twice a day — 32 calls/day total. Factor this into your X billing cap alongside the mentions/metrics flows.

nodes.name: Fetch Existing Candidates (GitHub)
nodes.notes: continueOnFail intentional: doesn't exist on the very first run.
